> [!NOTE]
> Emergency Intelligence AI is an independent open-source project. Official GSoC 2027 mentoring organizations will only be announced by Google in early 2027. This template helps contributors explore, scope, and prototype prospective project ideas.

## 1. Project Title & Abstract
A concise 2-3 sentence overview of the technical problem and proposed contribution.

## 2. Prospective Mentoring Organization Alignment
Which historical open-source geospatial/scientific organization best aligns with this idea?
- [ ] **OSGeo** (pgRouting, QGIS, GDAL, geometric algorithms)
- [ ] **Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT) / OSMF** (disaster routing, accessibility)
- [ ] **NumFOCUS** (scientific Python, graph data structures, benchmarking)
- [ ] **Python Software Foundation (PSF)** (standard library implementations)
- [ ] Other: `<specify>`

## 3. Technical Scope & Architecture
- **Target Component:** (e.g. Turn restriction dual graphs, Dynamic flood polygon exclusion, Multi-facility triage dispatch)
- **Constraint Compliance:** Explain how this proposal strictly maintains **zero external runtime dependencies** (standard Python library only).

## 4. Measurable Deliverables & Milestones
- **Milestone 1 (Foundations & Data Model):**
- **Milestone 2 (Core Algorithm & Tests):**
- **Milestone 3 (Benchmarks & Demo):**

## 5. Testing & Evaluation Strategy
How will correctness and performance be quantitatively measured? (e.g., nodes explored, rerouting latency in ms, branch coverage $\ge 90\%$).

## 6. Contributor Background & Upstream Engagement
Briefly mention your prior experience, PRs, or areas of interest in open-source routing and GIS.
